articles.title: India operationally deploys nuclear warheads on submarines for first time, SIPRI reports
articles.summary: India has successfully deployed a submarine equipped with nuclear warheads for patrol, a significant enhancement to its strategic deterrent capabilities. This development reinforces India's second-strike capacity as a responsible nuclear power. The move reflects evolving geopolitical dynamics and strengthens India's national security posture in a complex global environment, demonstrating its commitment to maritime defence and strategic autonomy.

articles.title: India is quietly putting its nuclear arsenal on a shorter fuse
articles.summary: The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) Yearbook 2026 reveals India has, for the first time, operationally deployed 12 nuclear warheads. This significant development, published in June, indicates a notable shift in India's nuclear posture. It highlights ongoing advancements and strategic considerations in the nation's defence capabilities, as observed by a leading global security think tank.

articles.title: Delhi briefly placed on high security alert after hoax threat call to blow up the Red Fort
articles.summary: Delhi experienced a high-security alert following a threat call claiming the historic Red Fort would be blown up. Security forces promptly responded, cordoning the area and investigating. The call was later confirmed as a hoax, leading to the alert's withdrawal. This incident highlights the swift response of security agencies and robust protocols protecting national heritage sites, even against false alarms, ensuring public safety.

articles.title: Future wars will still be won by resolve and soldiers, not just AI: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh
articles.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, in Visakhapatnam, stated that while Artificial Intelligence may characterize future wars, victory will ultimately hinge on national resolve, well-trained soldiers, and robust military power. He emphasized that technology acts as a force multiplier, but human courage and conventional strength remain paramount for national security, urging preparedness against evolving threats.

articles.title: China leaps ahead with reusable rocket booster, India’s NGLV years away
articles.summary: China has advanced its space capabilities with reusable rocket boosters, signifying a lead in this critical technology. In contrast, India's Next Generation Launch Vehicle (NGLV) is still several years from development. This highlights a technology gap and emphasizes the need for accelerated research in India's space program to keep pace with global developments.
